chapter: Blackbirds, Carmen Jones and the Ziegfeld Follies
title: After Blackbirds: vaudeville dates, Nazarro still booking, then Ziegfeld
summary: They took the Plantation circuit and California in 1929 and returned in 1931 for the Follies, still booked by Nazarro until their break around 1943-45; Bubbles takes whatever is best.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: When we finished the "Blackbirds" we go and do a couple more dates in vaudeville and this was 1929 and I think we took the Plantation circuit down, I'm not sure. It was the Plantation circuit we took out then, in '29 and went to California and come back to New York to join Ziegfeld Follies in '31.
Nazarro was booking you, wasn't he?
So there still was a relationship at that time.
Yeah, I hadn't broken that up yet. I've got to go to Germany before I break that up. That breaks up in 1943 or '45.
I would imagine that a Broadway show like "Blackbirds" provided a different type of environment for you to perform
in that was different from the vaudeville circuit that you were --
It was a show. It was a show.
But I mean it was something probably a lot more exciting for you in a sense because you had a different environment to perform in.
Were you attempting to do other things like that at this time?
I was doing the first thing that come along that was best for me. First thing that come along that was the best I thought I could do at this time.
